reviewer: independent Opus agent, read-only, fresh context (round 2, tool change only)

findings.finding: The new test's Tier A check passed without testing anything: it ran with use_jev=False, where Tier A is always empty.
findings.resolution: fixed: the test now runs with the reckless Jev stand-in (Tier A exists), asserts the Tier A header has no evidence column, that Tier B keeps it, and that Tier C is a count. Mutation check: putting the evidence column back into Tier A makes the test fail; the changed code passes (13 passed).

findings.finding: With zero Tier C items the short report still said 'Not listed here ... run with --full', which suggests hidden items.
findings.resolution: fixed: the sentence is shown only when Tier C is non-empty; otherwise 'None.'

findings.finding: The eval command has no --full option, and evaluate.py writes and copies the short report, so the committed demo run/report.md (old layout) no longer matches what the tool writes.
findings.resolution: accepted for this run, not fixed: the eval copy is a report of the same run and the tiers are unchanged; the old run/report.md in the JEV repo is not edited (read-only rule). Listed in manifest deviations.

findings.finding: With MAX_C_LINES removed, --full lists every Tier C item (no 60-line cap and no '... N more' line).
findings.resolution: accepted: the opt-in --full is explicit and meant to list everything.
